prior_dispositions.R1-A: partly implemented: held 72–96 tick roots and 48 tick peak phrase endings; edge/contrast foundations remain short and final landing register is abrupt
prior_dispositions.R1-B: partly implemented: no exact scene1/5 or3/6 duplicates; scene5 reversal does not move original timestamps; peak internal halves still closely repeat and long spans need stronger sentences
prior_dispositions.R1-C: partly implemented: real evolving build locks, late attack withdrawal, subtractive contrasts and cadences; Neon repeats its full cadence and restarts drums
prior_dispositions.R1-D: partly implemented: changed harmonic starting points, written cadences and scene6 inversion; no common-tone optimization, triads not inverted
prior_dispositions.R1-E: partly implemented: longer phrase endpoints and sparser replies; generic reply grid overlaps main attacks in Packet/Neon and register transform wraps
prior_dispositions.R1-F: partly implemented: supported lock lanes now trace scene arcs; all songs still share the main modulation topology and need phrase-specific identity
prior_dispositions.R1-G: timing defect implemented: 192 tick input gate spans four 48 tick arp intervals; wide simultaneous chord-swell proposal unresolved
prior_dispositions.R1-H: partly implemented: contrast sections have purposeful different drum subtraction; distinct space-themed phrase gestures remain limited

issues.R2-A: Write explicit register-aware phrase transformations. Reversal must move pitches onto chosen new onsets; scene-6 modulo-seven must not accidentally fold octave information or alter the preserved hook head. Verify actual serialized chronological notes, not comments.
issues.R2-B: Use per-song call/answer placement. Packet has main/answer onset collisions at step 5 in first peak and 2/10 in second; Neon second peak also collides at 2/10. Layering can be valid, but do not claim those events occupy lead rests. Compose a two-phrase sentence and a distinct eighth-bar ending. Afterglow Hook2 also has 8 simultaneous main/answer onsets at step10 across its eight bars.
issues.R2-C: Resolve Event Horizon chord identity. Gate repair is accepted; an UpDown arp serializes a chord. The original sustained/short wide chord-swell proposal needs a simultaneous chord layer or an explicitly reasoned alternative. Four 8-bar repetitions require internal 8-bar development, not necessarily occurrence automation.
issues.R2-D: Complete harmonic voice-leading and endings. Inversion of one stack is a useful change but not smooth voice-leading; retain common tones/select nearest register deliberately. Prepare low-register tonic landings. Neon needs one directional eight-bar exit rather than restarting its completed cadence.
issues.R2-E: Differentiate signature gestures musically: Afterglow sustained drift/common tones, Event suspension then wide release, Packet short transmission interruption and resolving chromatic approach if retaining that promise, Neon sung phrase and returning pulse. Shared two-lane build curves do not fully express four identities.

scenes.name: Intro
scenes.fix: Intro remains four bars of the same edge texture; stage the bass and distant reply, sustain one foundation, and give bar 4 a recognisable pickup. Preserve its gentle scale and swing.

scenes.name: Verse
scenes.fix: Held 72-tick bass roots now ground the groove. Give the two-note verse fragment a two-bar destination and smooth the chord tops with common tones; the unchanged root-position blocks still leap with every root.

scenes.name: Lift
scenes.fix: The four-bar lock rise and final release are real. Shape the harmonic top line toward the hook and keep the final withdrawal gentle; a last-bar timbre drop alone is a largely shared build recipe.

scenes.name: Hook
scenes.fix: The 48-tick fourth-bar endpoint is an improvement. Compose a complementary second four-bar sentence instead of replaying the first with the same bar-4 fill; allow one longer warm chord/lead suspension to settle into A.

scenes.name: Bridge
scenes.fix: Kick removal for bars 1–4 and sparse returning markers create the intended release. Thin the two chord attacks per bar and lengthen a common tone so the bridge drifts instead of remaining a stab pattern beneath sparse drums.

scenes.name: Vrs2
scenes.fix: The bass rhythm and selected lead fragment differ from Verse. Reversing tuples with their original timestamps is not reordering the phrase: assign new onsets to the reordered notes, then prepare the next hook with its final two bars.

scenes.name: Hook2
scenes.fix: The inversion and late lift distinguish Hook2. Keep the original hook head, explicitly voice the later answer, and make its last two bars resolve rather than merely increase brightness; chord stacks still move as parallel blocks.

scenes.name: Outro
scenes.fix: The C–F–G–Am cadence and held A are purposeful. Keep the final tonic in a related lead register or prepare the current low-register drop, and make the final chord sustain/release fit the intended drift before Stop.

scenes.name: Intro
scenes.fix: The twice-repeated intro still uses the edge snare at step 12 while the song identity uses step 8. Choose a deliberate pickup displacement or establish the half-time backbeat earlier; build entrance roles across the eight-bar span.

scenes.name: Verse
scenes.fix: The held low roots help the half-time frame. Let the pickup and reply alternate across two bars, and distinguish its chord articulation from the more connected drop.

scenes.name: Build
scenes.fix: The subdivision tightening and final attack withdrawal now deliver a build. Keep the final gap free of sustained crossing notes, and use a chord-register/envelope change to prepare the broad harmonic payoff rather than only two shared lock lanes.

scenes.name: Drop
scenes.fix: 192-tick input holds and full arp gates fix early truncation. They produce connected serial arpeggiation, not simultaneous wide chord swells. Realize the promised chord hook with the arp disabled on its slot, or explicitly justify a different musical proposal; shape an eight-bar question/answer for the four repetitions.

scenes.name: Break
scenes.fix: The kickless break and two sparse bass notes are a convincing reset. Expose a held chord/common tone or lone reply for one phrase, then stage the pickup into Vrs2 instead of returning all voices together.

scenes.name: Vrs2
scenes.fix: New bass placement and changed fragment count as development. Explicitly remap phrase onsets and write a final-bar approach into Drop2; chronological sorting defeats the claimed reversed ordering.

scenes.name: Drop2
scenes.fix: The register wrap changes the first F5 to F4 even before the intended second-half shift. Write explicit pitches/registers, retain the recognizable hook head, realize wide chord support, and make bars 5–8 a true answer so four identical launches remain purposeful.

scenes.name: Outro
scenes.fix: The Ab–Db–Eb–Fm cadence and tonic closure improve the exit. Prepare the low F landing from the upper lead and allow the harmonic resolution to hold long enough to register before the tail/Stop.

scenes.name: Intro
scenes.fix: The high/low pluck identity remains the strongest opener, but stage its four-bar entry and ground the high fragment with one held root. Use a rest before A-side rather than continuous shared edge activity.

scenes.name: A-side
scenes.fix: Root sustain improves the elastic bass. Compose an actual two-bar call/answer with different onset ownership, plus one brief chromatic approach that resolves immediately if retaining that original proposal; do not treat out-of-key fifth doubling as that gesture.

scenes.name: Build
scenes.fix: Build locks now evolve, and the final gap is present. Add one specifically placed pitch/decay or register interruption as the promised packet-like gesture, supported by the existing effects rather than another common brightness swell.

scenes.name: Bloom
scenes.fix: Track 7 attacks step 5 while the main lead attacks step 5: these are layered notes, not a rest-based answer. Move the answer into a real gap and differentiate the second four bars through register exchange or a short dropout.

scenes.name: Glitch
scenes.fix: Sparse isolated drums make Glitch a real interruption. Now create a short whole-ensemble rest or one displaced fragment with an explicit return cue; steady chord/bass/lead entries still make the edit feel like ordinary subtraction.

scenes.name: B-side
scenes.fix: Changed bass and selected lead fragment are useful. Actually exchange high/low call and answer roles; reversing the tuple list preserves timestamps. Give the last two bars a clear return cue.

scenes.name: Bloom2
scenes.fix: The extra chord attack, changed stack and brighter later half supply development. Avoid track-7 collisions at steps 2/10, write the register exchange explicitly and reserve one distinct end-of-phrase gesture.

scenes.name: Outro
scenes.fix: F–Bb–C–Dm with held low D is a clearer destination. Prepare the high-to-low handoff, progressively expose the warble tail, and avoid leaving the final chord more clipped than its closing lead.

scenes.name: Intro
scenes.fix: Two identical four-bar intro entries still establish little direction. Encode an eight-bar introduction or write a sufficiently shaped single passage; keep the straight kick/offbeat-hat identity as the eventual entrance.

scenes.name: Verse
scenes.fix: 72-tick bass anchors improve pulse. Make the sparse verse motive a sung two-bar sentence and smooth chord voicings rather than relying on root-position leaps.

scenes.name: Pre
scenes.fix: The rising curve and final withdrawal work. Let the chord top lead into the refrain and make the last bar a clear pre-chorus suspension/release, preserving the compact electropop pace.

scenes.name: Chorus
scenes.fix: The held phrase ending helps, but bars 5–8 repeat bars 1–4. Write an answering contour/held resolution and reserve a different fill or subtraction for the eighth bar so three launches have an internal journey.

scenes.name: Bridge
scenes.fix: The kickless bridge is implemented. Give the exposed chord/lead register a contrast too, with a short melodic silence and a prepared drum return rather than unchanged stab rhythm under absent kick.

scenes.name: Vrs2
scenes.fix: The new bass rhythm and selected fragment distinguish Vrs2. Explicit onset remapping is needed for the claimed reversal, and a concluding pickup should carry its last phrase into the final chorus.

scenes.name: Chor2
scenes.fix: The modulo transposition turns the E5 hook note into A4 and the held ending into C5 over Em7; this may be an intentional suspended variation, but it is not a fourth-up answer. Write a register-aware contour and resolution, and move simultaneous track-7 attacks at steps 2/10 into actual gaps.

scenes.name: Outro
scenes.fix: A complete four-bar cadence now works once, but the chain repeats it and restarts drums after closure. Make a single eight-bar outro whose second half stays thinned and closes once, or shorten/rebalance the chain deliberately.
